# Resizable

Panels people resize by dragging the line between them.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Content first</span> Resizable panels are for desktop tools, not phones. Content first readers arrive on phones and laptops alike, and it avoids data-heavy tools. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./sheet">Sheet</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Desktop tools where people choose how much space each panel gets.
- **Not when:** Phones, or layouts with one obvious shape.

Instead:

- [Sidebar](./sidebar.md): Fixed app navigation.

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | The handle can be focused and moved with arrow keys. | undefined |



## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add resizable
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Resizable reads 3 of Content first's tokens. Each row follows one part of the component from its class to the value it ends at, in every theme. Change a token in the scheme and every component that reads it follows.
